question: Should an authorized elevated-full invocation be allowed to bypass a matching `tools.exec.denylist` STOP rule?
rationale: The answer defines the permanent security contract between an operator-authored persisted STOP policy and the existing elevated execution capability; it cannot be safely inferred from tests or contributor intent alone.

options.title: Preserve deny-over-allow
options.body: Require a one-shot human approval for denylist hits even when elevated-full is authorized, so configured STOP rules always interrupt execution.

options.title: Accept break-glass bypass
options.body: Keep the elevated-full exception, but explicitly approve it as a documented operator-facing break-glass contract and retain focused coverage for that precedence.

recommendation.title: Preserve deny-over-allow
recommendation.body: Require a one-shot human approval for denylist hits even when elevated-full is authorized, so configured STOP rules always interrupt execution.

likelyOwner.reason: The discussion identifies exec-security ownership for this policy boundary.
